findings.reason: the change section would key the exception on the existing `unintegrated` field instead of adding a field to a dataclass whose own docstring says only `binding` must be acted on.
findings.text: §5 says `ClaimDisposition` "gains a `stopped` flag beside `binding` (it already tells the two cases apart, but only in its reason text)", but the cited class already carries `unintegrated: tuple[str, ...]` (reckon/crew/node.py:1497), which is non-empty exactly for the stopped-holder-holding-work case and empty for running, pid-less and stopped-and-empty, so the disposition already distinguishes the two cases structurally and the planned flag duplicates `unintegrated`

findings.reason: the change must name how the fact reaches that second site (carried on `_LiveScopeClaim` from the same disposition) or state that the exception is confined to the dispatch route.
findings.text: §5 states each `_RepositoryScopeClaim` carries the holder's run id and stopped state "read from `claim_disposition`", but `_RepositoryScopeClaim` has a second construction site, the registry facade in `reckon/crew/runs.py:1198-1215`, which rebuilds the claims from `_LiveScopeClaim` and never calls `claim_disposition` (it does not carry `binding` across either, so that field defaults True there), so the new stopped fact would sit at its default on that route and the exception would not apply where that facade is the check
